title: The wedding feast
hookLine: a meal to celebrate, even with one sheep (Bukhari)

lines: A TRACE OF YELLOW ON HIS CLOTHES.
HOLD A MEAL, EVEN WITH ONE SHEEP.
cards: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf walks into Medina with a trace of yellow on his clothes, the color of a perfume, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ notices. What's this? I've married a woman of the Ansar, he says.
The Prophet asks what he gave her. A date stone's weight of gold. Then the Prophet tells him the next thing to do.
Not buy a house. Not throw a party to impress the town. In Sahih al-Bukhari, his words come down to this: hold a wedding meal, even if it's only one sheep.
The marriage is made. Now feed people. Today's word: walimah.

teach.b: Walimah is the wedding feast, the meal that celebrates and announces a marriage. The nikah needed a public celebration; this is it, served on plates. First, the size.
Even one sheep. The point isn't the menu. It's that there should be a meal at all, shared, so the marriage is known and the joy is passed around.
Second, what a feast can look like.

teach.h: DATES AND BUTTER ON A LEATHER MAT.
teach.b: In Bukhari, the companion Anas describes a wedding meal the Prophet gave with no bread and no meat at all: dates, dried yogurt and butter, spread on a leather mat. Third, who's at the table.

teach.h: THE WORST FOOD: RICH IN, POOR OUT.
teach.b: A report in Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah, is blunt: the worst food is the food of a wedding feast where the rich are invited and the poor are left out. The walimah can be humble.
What it can't be, in that report, is a party that shuts the door on the poor. Fourth, the guests' side.
Bukhari also keeps the instruction that when someone is invited to a wedding feast, they should come. Showing up is part of it.
The schools discuss how strong these are: whether holding a walimah is required or strongly recommended, and when a guest may excuse himself. A marriage is made with words.

Then it's celebrated with food, and the guest list reaches past the people who can invite you back. The feast tells the town these two are married, and it turns a private joy into something a neighbor can taste.

how: After a nikah, a Muslim family may hold a walimah, a wedding meal for relatives, friends and neighbors, which may be a simple dinner at home or a large hall reception; guests who are invited are encouraged to attend.

practice: Bring to mind the best meal you ever shared, not the most expensive, the best: who was at the table, and what was on it? Notice how much of the memory is the food and how much is the people.
Then picture a simple table for one small good thing that hasn't been celebrated, and one person you'd invite who's rarely invited; if you pray, you can give thanks in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Walimah. The wedding feast, held to celebrate and announce a marriage, even if it's only one sheep, with the poor at the table too. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a feast, and especially the wedding meal that celebrates a marriage.

carryVoice: Your line: feed people. Even one sheep, even dates on a leather mat, with the poor invited. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 5167 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: hold a wedding meal, even with one sheep)

Sahih al-Bukhari 5177 (Abu Hurayrah: the worst food is a wedding feast for the rich without the poor)
Sahih al-Bukhari 5173 (when invited to a wedding feast, come)
